rows.patient_note: A 22-year-old female presents to the hospital with fatigue and recent headaches. She has a documented history of GERD, a kidney transplant, hypertension, evident with several recorded high blood pressure readings in the clinic. Moreover, she suffered a transient ischemic attack of her brain last year. She was solemn when she shared that she tends to drink more than moderately, admitting to a weekly average of 12 alcoholic beverages. In her medical history, there are suggestive signs of hepatic cirrhosis and confirmed renal disease. She denies using any medication known to exacerbate bleeding such as NSAIDs, anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents. Furthermore, there is no clear history of a major bleeding episode or any known coagulation disorders that predispose her to bleeding. The blood investigations, including coagulation studies, show a stable international normalized ratio (INR), and hemoglobin levels within range. The plan is to continue monitoring her closely and to adjust her therapies as needed based on the comprehensive assessment of her case.

mdcalc_rules: One point each, 0-9 total: Hypertension (uncontrolled, >160 mmHg systolic); Renal disease (dialysis, transplant, Cr >2.26 mg/dL or >200 umol/L); Liver disease (cirrhosis, or bilirubin >2x normal with AST/ALT/AP >3x normal); Stroke history; Prior major bleeding or predisposition to bleeding; Labile INR (unstable/high INRs, TTR <60%); Age >65; Medication usage predisposing to bleeding (aspirin, clopidogrel, NSAIDs); Alcohol use (>=8 drinks/week). MDCalc gives no definition beyond these descriptors; TIA is not listed under stroke, and anticoagulants are not listed as a drug point.
